concepts.name: Direct statements and pointing
concepts.description: Combine one or two steps into a single relation word; unwind "pointing" sentences from the speaker outwards.

concepts.name: Family-tree puzzles
concepts.description: Draw everyone once, by generation, with marriages and children, then read any relation off the tree.

concepts.name: Coded relations
concepts.description: Symbols stand for relations; decode the expression left to right into statements.

concepts.name: Generations
concepts.description: Parent–child links move one generation; spouses and siblings share a generation.

concepts.name: Gender ambiguity
concepts.description: A statement fixes only its subject’s gender; when the answer needs an unknown gender, it cannot be determined.

formulas.title: Combining two steps
formulas.prompt: How do you name a relation that goes through one middle person?
formulas.formula:
Father’s / mother’s brother = uncle; their sister = aunt
Father’s / mother’s father = grandfather
Brother’s / sister’s son = nephew; daughter = niece
Uncle’s or aunt’s child = cousin
formulas.explanation: Walk from the person asked about, one step at a time, and name the whole walk.
formulas.example: Meena is Arjun’s mother and Ravi is Meena’s brother: Ravi is Arjun’s uncle.
formulas.commonMistake: Answering the reverse question (how Arjun is related to Ravi).
formulas.applicationPrompt: X is the sister of Y, and Y is the father of Z. How is X related to Z?

formulas.title: Draw the tree
formulas.prompt: How do you set out a family-tree puzzle?
formulas.formula:
Square = man, circle = woman
Double line = married; line down = parent to child
One row per generation
formulas.explanation: Once the picture is drawn, every relation is a short walk on it.
formulas.example: Mohan = Kamala (top row); Suresh, Lata below; Arun, Bindu in the third row.
formulas.commonMistake: Starting to answer before every statement is on the drawing.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A is the wife of B, and C is the son of A. Draw the three people.

formulas.title: In-laws
formulas.formula:
Spouse’s parents = father-/mother-in-law
Child’s spouse = son-/daughter-in-law
Spouse’s sibling, or sibling’s spouse = brother-/sister-in-law
formulas.explanation: "In-law" relations always pass through exactly one marriage.
formulas.example: Vikram married Lata, Mohan’s daughter: Vikram is Mohan’s son-in-law.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Priya is the wife of Lata’s brother. How is Priya related to Lata?

formulas.title: Coded relations
formulas.prompt: How do you read an expression like P × Q + R?
formulas.formula:
Each symbol links the letter before it to the letter after it:
"P × Q" says what P is to Q
Decode left to right, drawing as you go
formulas.explanation: The expression is just a list of statements written in symbols.
formulas.example: + father, × brother: P × Q + R = P is Q’s brother, Q is R’s father ⇒ P is R’s uncle.
formulas.commonMistake: Reading a symbol the wrong way round (what Q is to P).
formulas.applicationPrompt: ÷ means daughter, − means wife. Decode "P ÷ Q − R".

formulas.title: Generations
formulas.formula:
Parent → child: one row down
Husband, wife, brother, sister: same row
Generations apart = difference in rows
formulas.explanation: Only parent–child links change the generation.
formulas.example: Grandmother and grandson are 2 generations apart.
formulas.commonMistake: Moving a husband or wife to a different row.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A is B’s father and C is B’s wife. How many generations do A, B and C span?

formulas.title: Where gender comes from
formulas.prompt: When is a person’s gender known?
formulas.formula:
Only from the word used for that person (father, sister, wife, …)
or from a marriage (a wife’s husband is male)
"Child", "parent", "sibling" and being the object of a statement say nothing
formulas.explanation: "A is the brother of B" tells you A is male and nothing about B.
formulas.example: Neel is the brother of Kavi: Kavi could be Neel’s brother or sister.
formulas.commonMistake: Guessing a gender from a name or a usual role.
formulas.applicationPrompt: P is the mother of Q. Is Q’s gender known?

formulas.title: "My father’s only son"
formulas.prompt: A man says "my father’s only son". Who is that?
formulas.formula:
Said by a man: himself
Said by a woman: her brother
(same for "my mother’s only daughter" said by a woman: herself)
formulas.explanation: A man is his father’s son; if there is only one son, it is him.
formulas.example: Arun: "the only son of my father’s father" is Arun’s father, since he is his grandfather’s son.
formulas.commonMistake: Treating the only son as a different person when the speaker is male.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Ravi says, "He is my father’s only son’s son." Who is "he" to Ravi?

formulas.title: Reverse a relation
formulas.prompt: If A is B’s uncle, how is B related to A?
formulas.formula:
Uncle/aunt ↔ nephew/niece
Grandparent ↔ grandchild
Father-/mother-in-law ↔ son-/daughter-in-law
The reverse needs B’s gender, not A’s
formulas.explanation: Going the other way changes the word and the gender it depends on.
formulas.example: Ravi is Arjun’s uncle, so Arjun is Ravi’s nephew (Arjun is male).
formulas.commonMistake: Keeping A’s gender in the reversed word.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Kamala is Uma’s grandmother. How is Uma related to Kamala?

levels.title: Families on Paper
levels.description: Walking from one person to another, drawing the tree, and gender.

blocks.title: Walk from the person asked about
blocks.body: "How is Ravi related to Arjun?" asks what Ravi is to Arjun. Start at Arjun and walk to Ravi one step at a time: Arjun’s mother is Meena, and Meena’s brother is Ravi. Mother’s brother is uncle, so Ravi is Arjun’s uncle. Answering the other way round (Arjun is Ravi’s nephew) is the most common slip.

blocks.title: Two steps, one word
blocks.body:
Parent’s brother = uncle   Parent’s sister = aunt
Sibling’s son = nephew   Sibling’s daughter = niece
Uncle’s or aunt’s child = cousin
blocks.caption: A parent’s husband or wife is the other parent.

blocks.title: Draw the tree, then read it
blocks.body: For longer sets, draw before you answer: a square for a man, a circle for a woman, a double line for a marriage and a line down to children, one row per generation. Brothers and sisters share parents, so join them under the same couple. Someone whose gender no statement gives stays a plain shape until a later statement settles it.

blocks.title: Coded relations
blocks.body: If P + Q means "P is the father of Q" and P × Q means "P is the brother of Q", then P × Q + R reads: P is Q’s brother, and Q is R’s father. So P is the brother of R’s father: R’s uncle.
"A is the brother of B" tells you A is male and nothing about B. If the answer depends on a gender no statement gives, the answer is "cannot be determined".

questions.question: How is Neha related to the man?

solutionSteps: "The only daughter of my mother" — Neha is her mother’s daughter, and there is only one.
So the man’s mother is Neha.

solutionSteps: My father’s father = my grandfather.
His only son = my father.
My father’s daughter = my sister.

questions.question: How is U related to Q?
questions.context:
1. P is the father of Q.
2. R is the wife of P.
3. S is the brother of Q.
4. T is the wife of S.
5. U is the daughter of T.
6. V is the son of Q.
7. W is the husband of Q.
questions.explanation: P (a man) and R are married; their children are Q (a woman, since W is her husband) and S. S and T are married, with a daughter, U. Q and W are married, with a son, V. U is the daughter of S’s wife T, so S is U’s father. S is Q’s brother, so U is Q’s brother’s daughter: Q’s niece.
solutionSteps: P–R at the top. Q is P’s child, and S is Q’s brother, so S is P’s son too.
W is Q’s husband, so Q is a woman; V is Q’s son. S’s wife is T; U is T’s daughter.
P (a man) and R are married; their children are Q (a woman, since W is her husband) and S. S and T are married, with a daughter, U. Q and W are married, with a son, V.
questions.method: A brother’s daughter is a niece.

questions.question: How is P related to R?
questions.context:
'P + Q' means 'P is the father of Q'.
'P − Q' means 'P is the wife of Q'.
'P × Q' means 'P is the brother of Q'.
'P ÷ Q' means 'P is the daughter of Q'.
Expression: P × Q + R
questions.explanation: P × Q: P is the brother of Q. Q + R: Q is the father of R. So P is the brother of R’s father: R’s uncle.
solutionSteps: Decode P × Q: P is Q’s brother.
Decode Q + R: Q is R’s father.
Father’s brother = uncle.
questions.method: Decode left to right; each symbol links the letters on either side of it.

hints.text: Write each symbol out as a sentence: "P × Q" says what P is to Q.
Then combine: P is the brother of R’s father.

commonMistakes: Reading "Q + R" as "R is the father of Q".

questions.question: How is R related to P?
questions.context:

'P − Q' means 'P is the wife of Q'.
'P × Q' means 'P is the brother of Q'.
'P ÷ Q' means 'P is the daughter of Q'.
Expression: P ÷ Q − R
questions.explanation: P ÷ Q: P is the daughter of Q. Q − R: Q is the wife of R. R is the husband of P’s mother, so R is P’s father.
solutionSteps: P ÷ Q: P is Q’s daughter (so Q is P’s parent).
Q − R: Q is R’s wife, so Q is a woman: P’s mother.
Mother’s husband = father.
questions.method: A parent’s husband or wife is the other parent.

hints.text: Decode both symbols first.
Q is P’s mother. Who is her husband?

commonMistakes: Answering "Husband": R is Q’s husband, but P’s father.

questions.question: How is R related to P?
questions.context:
'P + Q' means 'P is the father of Q'.
'P − Q' means 'P is the wife of Q'.
'P × Q' means 'P is the brother of Q'.
'P ÷ Q' means 'P is the daughter of Q'.
Expression: P + Q − R × S
questions.explanation: P + Q: P is Q’s father. Q − R: Q is R’s wife. R × S: R is S’s brother. R is married to P’s daughter Q, so R is P’s son-in-law. (S is not needed.)
solutionSteps: P + Q: P is the father of Q.
Q − R: Q (a woman) is the wife of R.
R is the husband of P’s daughter: son-in-law. R × S only says R has a sibling S.
questions.method: Decode every link, then use only the ones on the path between the two people asked about.

hints.text: Decode all three symbols.
Q is P’s daughter. Who is Q married to?

commonMistakes: Answering "Son" for a daughter’s husband.

questions.question: How is P related to S?
questions.context:
'P + Q' means 'P is the father of Q'.
'P − Q' means 'P is the wife of Q'.
'P × Q' means 'P is the brother of Q'.
'P ÷ Q' means 'P is the daughter of Q'.
Expression: P × Q ÷ R + S
questions.explanation: P × Q: P is Q’s brother. Q ÷ R: Q is R’s daughter. R + S: R is S’s father. So P, Q and S are all R’s children, and P (a man) is S’s brother.
solutionSteps: P × Q: P is Q’s brother, so P is male and shares Q’s parents.
Q ÷ R: Q is R’s daughter, so P is R’s child too.
R + S: S is R’s child. Children of the same parent are brothers and sisters: P is S’s brother.
questions.method: Siblings share parents; decode, then group the children.

hints.text: Decode each symbol; who are R’s children?
P’s gender comes from "brother".

commonMistakes: Answering "Uncle" by putting P a generation above S.

"Kavi is the child of Asha" gives no gender.
So Kavi is Neel’s brother or sister: cannot be determined.

questions.question: Whose gender can be determined from these statements? Select all that apply.
questions.context:
1. P is the father of Q.
2. R is the sister of Q.
3. S is the husband of R.
4. T is the child of S.
questions.explanation: P is a father (male), R a sister (female) and S a husband (male). Q is only ever the person someone else is related to, and T is only "the child", so their genders are unknown.
solutionSteps: Go person by person and look for a gendered word used for them.
P: father. R: sister. S: husband.
Q and T: no gendered word.
questions.method: Gender comes only from the word used for that person, or from a marriage.

hints.text: In "P is the father of Q", only P’s gender is known.
Check each of the five names in turn.

commonMistakes: Giving Q a gender from "R is the sister of Q".

questions.question: How is Kiran related to Mala?
questions.context: Pointing to Kiran, Mala (a woman) said, “Kiran’s father is my father’s only son.”
questions.explanation: Mala is a woman, so her father’s only son is her brother. Kiran’s father is Mala’s brother, so Kiran is Mala’s nephew or niece. Nothing says whether Kiran is a boy or a girl, so the answer cannot be determined.
solutionSteps: My father’s only son, said by a woman = my brother.
Kiran’s father is Mala’s brother.
Kiran is a nephew or a niece: Kiran’s gender is not given.
questions.method: Work out the relation, then check you know the gender it needs.

hints.text: Could Mala be her father’s son?
You can tell Kiran is a brother’s child. Can you tell if Kiran is a boy or a girl?

commonMistakes: Assuming Kiran is a boy and answering "Nephew".
Answering "Son" by treating Mala as the only son.

questions.question: How many generations of this family are named in the statements?
questions.context:
1. Mohan is the husband of Kamala.
2. Suresh is the son of Kamala.
3. Lata is the sister of Suresh.
4. Priya is the wife of Suresh.
5. Arun is the son of Priya.
6. Vikram is the husband of Lata.
7. Bindu is the daughter of Vikram.
questions.explanation: Mohan and Kamala are married; their children are Suresh and Lata. Suresh and Priya are married, with a son, Arun. Lata and Vikram are married, with a daughter, Bindu. Oldest first: Mohan, Kamala | Suresh, Lata, Priya, Vikram | Arun, Bindu. That is 3 generations.
solutionSteps: Husbands, wives, brothers and sisters share a generation.
Mohan and Kamala; then their children and the children’s spouses; then Arun and Bindu.
Three rows: 3 generations.
questions.method: One row per generation; only parent–child links move between rows.

hints.text: Draw it: a square for a man, a circle for a woman, a double line for a marriage, a line down from parents to children.
Spouses stay in the same row as each other.

commonMistakes: Putting Priya and Vikram in a row of their own because they married into the family.

questions.question: How many generations apart are R and U?
questions.context:
1. P is the father of Q.
2. R is the wife of P.
3. S is the brother of Q.
4. T is the wife of S.
5. U is the daughter of T.
6. V is the son of Q.
7. W is the husband of Q.
questions.explanation: P (a man) and R are married; their children are Q (a woman, since W is her husband) and S. S and T are married, with a daughter, U. Q and W are married, with a son, V. R is in the top generation (with P); U is a grandchild (with V). They are 2 generations apart.
solutionSteps: R is P’s wife: top row.
S, Q, T and W: middle row.
U and V: bottom row. R to U is 2 rows.
questions.method: Count rows, not people or links.

hints.text: Draw it: a square for a man, a circle for a woman, a double line for a marriage, a line down from parents to children.
Which row is R in, and which row is U in?

commonMistakes: Counting the links between R and U instead of the rows.
